AC3 ENUMERATION (sweep run under Python 3.12.13, the worktree venv; greps scoped to *.py because unscoped greps are swamped by ~1MB of vendored JS under src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor_assets/node_modules/).

RESULT: the population is closed and every member is already proxy-safe. Nothing to fix, no follow-ups filed.

1. `grep -rn --include='*.py' "isinstance(.*Supports" src/rebar` -> ZERO hits. The Protocol is never named literally at a call site; it is always passed indirectly as `_capability_present`'s `protocol` parameter.

2. Protocol inventory. Only two `Supports*` Protocols exist, both @runtime_checkable, both in _backend.py: SupportsLinks (:505), SupportsComments (:537). SupportsIncremental no longer exists in code. All other @runtime_checkable Protocols in the tree — Runner (llm/runner.py:156), BindingStoreProtocol (outbound_differ.py:211 and inbound_differ.py:88), TicketTransport (_backend.py:217), Backend (_backend.py:551), RichTextCodec (adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py:36) — have ZERO isinstance call sites in src/rebar.

3. Executable isinstance-against-Protocol sites: exactly TWO in the whole tree.
   - dispatch_apply_phases.py:188 (`if isinstance(client, protocol) or hasattr(client, member)`) — the capability dispatch, reached from 4 sites: dispatch_one.py:347, :602, :681, and dispatch_apply_phases.py:319. ALREADY proxy-hardened by the `or hasattr` disjunct (task a3fa). Confirmed safe.
   - _backend.py:213 — the body of `_TransportPortMeta.__instancecheck__`, which is `all(hasattr(instance, member) for member in _REQUIRED_TRANSPORT_MEMBERS)`. Because it overrides __instancecheck__, `isinstance(x, TicketTransport)` never takes typing's getattr_static path at all — proxy-safe by construction. It has zero executable call sites in src/rebar (the four TicketTransport isinstance mentions at _backend.py:135, 207, 237, 508 are all docstring prose).

4. Adjacent `hasattr`-based capability checks — same decide-whether-to-act shape, but proxy-safe because hasattr honours __getattr__: apply_outbound.py:199 and :225; fetcher.py:302, :597, :647, :688. dispatch_apply_phases.py:161-162 already names fetcher.py:597/647/688 as the shape it is deliberately consistent with.

5. No dynamic/string-form hazard: `getattr_static` appears only in prose (_backend.py:577, adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:177, adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py:110); no code calls it.

AC4: `_capability_present` is unchanged. On centralising the fallback for reuse — the answer is NO, recorded as a reasoned outcome rather than a follow-up ticket: there is exactly one dispatch expression in the tree, so there is no second caller to share a helper with, and extracting one now would be speculative. If a second capability-dispatch site is ever added, that is the moment to extract.

Landed as Gerrit change 1659.

compiled_state.description:
# ADR-0083's isinstance-only capability detection is unsafe on Python 3.12+

## The gap

ADR-0083 `docs/adr/0083-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md:193-197` prescribes: "Callers detect
a capability by an `isinstance`-guarded check against the backend ... capability is observed
via behavior, not structural introspection."

Since CPython 3.12 (gh-102433) a `@runtime_checkable` Protocol `isinstance` resolves members
with `inspect.getattr_static`, which deliberately does NOT see attributes served by
`__getattr__`. The prescribed check therefore returns a FALSE "capability absent" for any
dynamically-proxying object.

This is TEMPORAL DECAY with a version boundary, not an authoring error. Measured on the same
proxy object and Protocol: python3.11 -> `isinstance` True; python3.12 -> False. rebar's
requires-python is >=3.11 and CI runs 3.11/3.12/3.13
(`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:282`), so an isinstance-only guard is correct on one
supported interpreter and silently skips writes on another.

Task `a3fa-e8d4-f4aa-4b51` fixed this LOCALLY in `_capability_present`
(`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py:140-199`, guard at line 188:
`if isinstance(client, protocol) or hasattr(client, member)`). The ADR text was never changed;
this ticket is that follow-up, so the next caller reading the ADR does not reimplement the
hazard.

## Evidence already gathered (AC3 sweep, run under Python 3.12.13)

Sweep of `src/rebar` (`*.py`-scoped; unscoped greps are swamped by vendored JS under
`llm/workflow/editor_assets/node_modules/`):

- `grep -rn "isinstance(.*Supports" src/rebar` -> ZERO hits. The Protocol is always passed
  indirectly as `_capability_present`'s `protocol` parameter.
- Only two `Supports*` Protocols exist, both `@runtime_checkable`, both in `_backend.py`:
  `SupportsLinks:505`, `SupportsComments:537`.
- Exactly ONE executable isinstance-against-Protocol capability dispatch exists in the tree:
  `dispatch_apply_phases.py:188`, reached from 4 sites (`dispatch_one.py:347`, `:602`, `:681`,
  `dispatch_apply_phases.py:319`). It is ALREADY proxy-hardened by the `or hasattr` disjunct.
- The only other Protocol isinstance is `_TransportPortMeta.__instancecheck__`
  (`_backend.py:213`), whose body is `all(hasattr(...))` — proxy-safe by construction, and it
  has zero call sites in `src/rebar`.
- Six `hasattr`-based capability checks (`apply_outbound.py:199,225`;
  `fetcher.py:302,597,647,688`) are the same decide-whether-to-act shape but proxy-safe.

Conclusion: nothing to FIX. The population is closed and every member is already proxy-safe.
The remaining defect is the ADR TEXT, which still prescribes the unsafe shape.

## Plan

Documentation-only change to `docs/adr/0083-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md`.

Insert a new amendment blockquote immediately after the existing `SupportsIncremental`
amendment (which occupies lines 199-205), matching that block's established style —
`> **AMENDED by [rebar:5c21-f24a-f7f8-4a55].**` lead-in, full four-quad ticket id. The
amendment will:

1. State that `isinstance` against a `@runtime_checkable` Protocol is NECESSARY but NOT
   SUFFICIENT on Python 3.12+, citing `getattr_static` / gh-102433 and framing it as a version
   boundary that made previously-correct guidance unsafe.
2. Name the consequence: a decorator/wrapper/recording proxy transport HAS the capability but
   fails the check, so a conforming caller skips the write and reports the skip as DESIGNED —
   a silent soft failure.
3. Prescribe the sanctioned shape: `isinstance` primary, member-level `hasattr(obj, member)`
   fallback, and point at `_capability_present` as the reference implementation.
4. Record that the tree-wide sweep found no other affected site.

No source change. `_capability_present` keeps its current behaviour (AC4). Centralising the
fallback for reuse is explicitly NOT done: with a single dispatch expression in the tree there
is no second caller to share it, so extraction would be premature; this is recorded as the
reasoned outcome rather than a follow-up ticket.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — ADR-0083's capability-detection paragraph carries an amendment, in the ADR's own
      amendment style, stating isinstance is necessary-but-not-sufficient on 3.12+ and citing
      the `getattr_static` behaviour plus the proxying-transport consequence.
- [ ] AC2 — the amendment names the isinstance-primary + member-`hasattr`-fallback shape and
      cites `_capability_present` as the reference implementation.
- [ ] AC3 — the sweep enumeration above is recorded on this ticket and every site is confirmed
      proxy-safe or fixed.
- [ ] AC4 — `_capability_present` is unchanged; the centralisation question is answered
      explicitly rather than actioned inline.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` are green.
- [ ] the change is `Verified +1` on Gerrit before the ticket is closed.

## Verify

- `grep -rn --include='*.py' "isinstance(.*Supports" src/rebar` (expect no hits)
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_capability_guard_a3fa.py -q`

file_impact.reason: amend the isinstance-only capability-detection guidance for the Python 3.12 getattr_static behaviour
